basics.name: Mark A. Conway-Greenslade
basics.label: Software Architect & Technology Leader
basics.summary: Technology leader and polyglot software architect with 25+ years delivering complex systems across the private and public sectors in Europe and beyond. Extensive experience within diverse R&D environments such as quantum instrumentation, zero-knowledge cryptography, blockchain financial infrastructure and climate-science computing. At home setting technical strategy, advising c-suite executives and shaping the processes that let engineering organisations scale. Able to build a culture of trust where exceptional teams flourish. Embodies a leadership style grounded in values such as integrity, candour, kindness and humour. Of the view that technology should serve communities and the planet — as reflected in years devoted to climate research and decentralised finance. Member of the IEEE and the Central Bank Research Association.

work.summary: Driving software at an ETH spin-off that builds nanoscale microscopes based on quantum magnetometry. Guided the team's shift to a lightweight, structured agile process; designed and built controllers for photonic and magnetic devices; redesigned the desktop application; and championed the adoption of Rust across the in-house QS3 platform. Advising both the engineering team and the executive suite.

A hybrid role across an R&D company specialising in cryptography and distributed systems. As Rust engineer, built the genesis protocol and tooling for a biometric identity platform based on secure multi-party computation. As technical product owner, steered customer-facing projects including a regulated privacy-focused stablecoin and a privacy-preserving loyalty programme. As business development lead, represented the company at industry events, shaped strategy and tracked emerging trends.

Led R&D in a complex, high-visibility blockchain environment. Partnered with the Head of Engineering to fold research proofs of concept into the core product, and worked with a team of macro-economists to design a blockchain-enabled core banking platform built around an emerging financial standard. Hands-on Rust throughout, applying zero-knowledge cryptography to deliver a ZK rollup and a ZK light client.

work.company: Institut Pierre Simon Laplace @ La Sorbonne
work.summary: Worked at the heart of climate research, extending the IPSL's HPC simulation environment with a real-time, event-driven messaging platform powering automated documentation, live monitoring, performance analytics and machine intelligence. Technical lead of es-doc.org, an international climate-model documentation project, and a driver of process change across the institute.

Part of the global team that delivered a layer-1 blockchain platform built on DAG-based proof-of-stake consensus. Designed and implemented an event-driven, scalable fuzz-testing platform for surfacing consensus flaws, and streamlined platform integration for external partners. Also led the professional-services team and mentored executives.

Helped build a decentralised finance ecosystem for a Zug start-up. Delivered a GraphQL trading API, a feature-rich command-line application, a multi-chain digital wallet and a Vue.js front end, while mentoring junior colleagues and reviewing ecosystem design.

Drove technology and process change in the Swiss arm of a global IT services company: introduced agile practice — Scrum, XP, CI/CD — designed a .NET SOA framework and mentored a seven-person development team.
Designed and led development of an interoperable B2B order-processing web service, applying .NET 3.0, domain-driven design and SOA. Also designed a rules-based workflow engine.
Designed and led development of a high-volume, real-time enrolment service for a US insurance provider, using an n-tier architecture with WCF communication between tiers.
Migrated C++ systems to .NET 2.0 under an agile process, and built web services sharing real-time automotive diagnostics across a suite of listening applications. Scrum, XP and TDD throughout.
Full-stack .NET engineer on a sales and management information system, covering architecture and design, web development, testing and deployment.

work.company: Securicor Systems · SSRADU · 3S Electronic Publishing · Customer Interface · Cap Gemini
work.summary: Software engineering and architecture roles across the UK, spanning n-tier client-server systems, COM frameworks in Visual Basic, database design and technical authorship. Highlights include architecting central London's traffic-violation adjudication system at the head of a twelve-person team (Securicor) and delivering Europe's largest IBM AS-400 project (Cap Gemini).

other.residency: UK citizen with Swiss Residency Permit
